section.broken: This section did not open. You can move to another one from the menu and come back later.
signin.title: Sign in
signin.body: The panel needs an account. You can create one the first time you sign in.
account.aria: The account you signed in with
connecting.note: You can leave this page open. The service may be starting from zero while the panel is already visible.
pending.title: Account waiting
pending.body: Signing in worked. The account is not enabled yet: a person has to approve it.
pending.note: There is nothing to do from here. This page will not change on its own: reload it once the approval has happened.
proposals.title: To approve
proposals.note: Approving shows nothing straight away: what you approve is set aside. The house takes it on its next run, and prints it or puts it on the display.
proposals.unreadable: I cannot read the proposals right now.
proposals.decideFailed: I could not record the decision. Try again later.
proposals.withdrawn: Withdrawn. It will not be delivered again. A sheet already printed stays in the house: it cannot be called back from here.
proposals.withdrawFailed: I could not record the withdrawal. Try again later.
experiences.title: Activities
experiences.note: A whole activity, devised for this house: something on the display, a sheet on the table, and what comes back off the scanner decides how it goes on. You approve the activity, not each step.
experiences.laterNote: There is no way to ask for one from here: the house asks, when it is its moment. Approving writes a row and nothing else — the house finds it at its next request, and decides for itself when to begin.
experiences.unreadable: I cannot read the activities right now.
experiences.asks: the rest is written at that moment
experiences.wayOut: It can end from here in {minutes} minutes:
experiences.noneApproved: None approved. Until there is one, the house has nothing to begin.
experiences.decideFailed: I could not record the decision. Try again later.
experiences.withdrawn: Withdrawn. It will not be handed over again. An activity already begun goes on by itself: all that can be done from here is move the hour it is over by.
experiences.sayingNote: From here you can move the hour it is over by, or bring that hour to now. It is not a way to stop it: the activity still reaches its ending, from wherever it got to. Nothing appears on any display.
experiences.saidWaiting: Written down. The house finds it at its next request, within a minute.
experiences.sayFailed: I could not record it. Try again later.
themes.title: Picture themes
themes.note: The display draws a new picture on one of these themes. You approve the theme, not each image: what you remove is no longer used.
themes.removeFailed: I could not remove the theme. Try again later.
themes.unreadable: I cannot read the themes right now.
themes.empty: No themes. While the list is empty the display uses the starting ones.
reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.note: What should be remembered, written the way you would say it. One thing per line, with the day and the hour if it has one: “brush teeth after dinner”, “Wednesday take the bin out”.
reminders.laterNote: Writing one down starts nothing: the panel cannot ask what a sentence means at the moment you write it. The house is the side that asks, on its next request.
reminders.placeholder: for example: brush teeth after dinner
reminders.removeFailed: I could not remove it. Try again later.
reminders.saveFailed: I could not save the change. Try again later.
reminders.notRead: The house has not read this one yet.
reminders.words: On the display you will read one of these:
reminders.noHour: The house found no hour in this sentence. Write it again with one in it.
reminders.unreadable: I cannot read the reminders right now.
guidelines.title: What it may change
guidelines.note: An activity does not always go the way it was written. Here you decide how far the house may depart from it on its own, without asking. One thing per line, the way you would say it: “going out into the garden is fine”, “it may print as many times as it needs”. What you do not write stays out: the house does not take it.
guidelines.laterNote: Writing here starts nothing. The house reads these lines at the moment it has to decide, inside an activity that has already begun.
guidelines.placeholder: for example: going out into the garden is fine
guidelines.suggestGarden: Going out into the garden is fine
guidelines.suggestPrinter: It may print as many times as it needs
guidelines.suggestScissors: The scissors are in the first drawer
guidelines.empty: Nothing written. The house stays at its narrowest: it changes only what the rules below let it change.
guidelines.oursNote: These hold in every household and cannot be changed from here:
guidelines.ours1: It never says anything about the person: not how well it went, not how much effort it took, not what any of it would suggest.
guidelines.ours2: It never announces, explains or apologises for a change of course. It arrives as part of what is happening.
guidelines.ours3: An ending stays reachable from wherever the activity has got to, and an ending reached early is the same ending.
guidelines.ours4: It uses only what this house has. It never invents materials, equipment or a place.
guidelines.ours5: Nothing can be failed and nothing has to be finished.
guidelines.unreadable: I cannot read it right now.
guidelines.saveFailed: I could not save it. Try again later.
rhythm.title: Rhythm
rhythm.note: When the display may change its picture, how often, and on which days an activity may begin. The house reads the choice on its next run: saving here starts nothing and wakes no device.
rhythm.timeZonePlaceholder: type a city or a country
rhythm.timeZoneUnknown: From here there is no telling what time it is in the house.
rhythm.timeZoneNote: Type the first letters of the city or the country and pick from the list. The clock beside it is the time the house will keep: check it against a clock in the room, and it follows summer time by itself. The country is in your language; the city keeps the English spelling the timezone database gives it, because the browser has no other. Leave it empty and the house uses its own machine's clock.
rhythm.beginNote: Overrides the day and the hour, not the evening pause. An activity already under way is not interrupted.
rhythm.beginAsked: Noted. The house finds it at its next look, within a minute.
rhythm.beginFailed: I could not note it. Try again later.
rhythm.afternoonNote: With no day chosen, nothing begins. On a chosen day the house looks once, after that hour, and begins the oldest approved activity — if there is one, and if the whole of it is over before the pause. It keeps no count of the ones that happened.
rhythm.wakeNote: On battery the display wakes about every ten minutes: below that spacing some pictures are generated and nobody sees them.
rhythm.saved: Saved. The house applies it on its next run.
rhythm.saveFailed: I could not save it. Try again later.
rhythm.unreadable: I cannot read the rhythm right now.
rhythm.quietOff: No pause: the picture may change at any hour.
preferences.title: Interests and difficulty
preferences.note: What the content is about and how demanding it is. The difficulty is a property of the material, not of whoever receives it. The house reads these choices on its next run: saving here starts no generation.
preferences.languageNote: The language of the content, on paper and on the display. It does not follow the language of this page: content approved in one language is not approved in another.
preferences.saved: Saved. The house applies it on its next run.
preferences.saveFailed: I could not save it. Try again later.
preferences.unreadable: I cannot read the settings right now.
devices.title: Devices
devices.note: Everything the house can use, with a job you choose and a name you write. Faults appear here: nothing of the kind ever appears on the displays in the house.
devices.unreadable: I cannot read the devices right now.
devices.nameNote: The name is the one that gets read out, so keep it to {limit} characters and to something recognisable. Do not put anybody's name in it.
devices.jobNote: A device can have several jobs, and the same job can sit on several devices: when there is more than one, the house picks between them each time.
devices.removeNote: Removing is not permanent: the house looks again on its own every five minutes, and a printer or scanner still switched on comes back to the list. What is lost is the jobs you had given it, which you assign again.
devices.saveFailed: I could not save that. Try again later.
devices.nameRefused: The house did not take this name: it carries the name of a person, and that never goes into what is written for the display. Write a name for the object instead.
job.remind: shows reminders when they are due
pictures.title: Pictures
pictures.note: Every picture that has appeared on the display, newest first. They are shown as the display shows them: two levels only, no greys.
pictures.unreadable: I cannot read the pictures right now.
pictures.empty: No pictures yet. The first arrives when the display asks for one.
pictures.downloadSince.none: No picture from that day onwards.
pictures.downloadSince.failed: I could not gather the pictures.
pictures.again.asked: Asked for. The house puts it up the next time it changes the picture.
pictures.again.failed: I could not write down the request.
usage.title: Usage
usage.note: What the models consumed this month. These are numbers about machines, not about a person, and not a target to reach.
usage.unreadable: I cannot read the usage right now.
usage.limit.note: How many model calls this house may make in a month. Not a spending budget: it is there to stop a loop that has lost its mind. An ordinary month spends about 1116. Saving here starts nothing and stops nothing: it applies from the next request on.
usage.limit.bounds: Above the calls already made this month, and at most {max}.
usage.limit.refused: I did not save it. It must be above {spent} (the calls already made this month) and no more than {max}.
limit.title: The house has reached its limit
limit.what: This month the house made {spent} model calls and the limit is {limit}. From now every request is refused: no new pictures, no pages read, no activity.
limit.why: This is not a spending budget you chose: it is there to stop a loop that has lost its mind. An ordinary month spends about 1116 calls, so either the house did far more than usual, or something jammed.
limit.failed: I could not raise it. It must be between the calls already made and {max}.
limit.done.title: Limit raised
limit.done: It is now {limit} calls a month. The house carries on at the next thing it asks for: the panel does not wake it.
error.title: It did not work
error.noAuth: The panel has no sign-in configuration yet.
error.signin: Signing in did not complete. Reload the page and try again.
admin.signin.title: Sign in
admin.signin.body: This page uses the workforce identity, not the one a parent signs in with. They are separate accounts even when the same person holds both.
admin.notAdmin.title: No role
admin.notAdmin.body: Signing in worked. This account holds no administrator role: it is assigned in the directory, not from here.
admin.notConfigured.title: Not configured
admin.notConfigured.body: The panel has no administrator identity yet. Until it does, this page can do nothing.
admin.waiting.title: Sign-ups waiting
admin.waiting.note: Admitting enables the panel for that address. It generates nothing and notifies nobody: whoever is admitted finds out by reloading their page.
admin.waiting.unreadable: I cannot read the sign-ups right now.
